transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/time: 2026-09-01 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Arcadia Infra Lead), Sofia Alvarez (Arcadia Sec), Priya Nair (Arcadia VP Eng)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery focused on private/VPC deployment options and networking constraints.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we, uh appreciate the time. quick intro, i'm maya, i run enterprise for redwood. diego's our solutions engineer.
[00:18] Liam Chen: hi all, liam here. we're trying to evaluate private deploy for data residency and latency, want to understand net ops impacts.
[00:30] Diego Ramos: great. quick overview \u2014 redwood private gives you a control plane outside your VPC but a data plane in your VPC using private endpoints or peering depending on cloud. ping me if i mangle any product names, sometimes the transcript calls it \"redwood dedecate\" heh.
[00:50] Priya Nair: our main guardrails: no public egress for inference traffic, keys must be customer-managed, and we want region-local inference for GDPR and latency.
[01:05] Sofia Alvarez: and from sec: SOC2 plus client audits, audit logs must be forwarded to our SIEM, SAML SSO + RBAC required. any HSM/KMS integration?
[01:20] Diego Ramos: yes on KMS. we integrate with customer KMS for model keys and storage encryption, HSM via your cloud provider's KMS/HSM offering. for logs we can push audit events to your endpoint or S3 with lifecycle, depends on retention.
[01:40] Liam Chen: network specifics \u2014 we run multi-account AWS, prefer Transit Gateway for central routing. we can't overlap CIDRs, we have limited spare /16 space, we want guidance on ENI counts and IP usage.
[02:00] Diego Ramos: got it. two typical patterns: 1) VPC peering/direct routing where we place inference workloads in your VPC (requires cross-account peering or an account we deploy into) 2) PrivateLink/private endpoint model where you call a private endpoint in your VPC to reach runtime \u2014 both avoid public internet. peering can be simpler for high throughput but needs CIDR non-overlap; PrivateLink avoids CIDR issues but has limits on connections and can add per-hour NLB costs.
[02:30] Maya Patel: and dedicated is an option if you want reserved GPU pools, otherwise hosted + private endpoint can be cost efficient but may not meet the isolation SLA.
[02:48] Priya Nair: our compliance team insisted on no shared tenancy for PII workloads. would Dedicated + Private VPC be the right combo?
[03:03] Diego Ramos: yes Dedicated in your VPC or a dedicated account with VPC peering can meet that. we also support an on-prem package if you need air-gapped.
[03:20] Sofia Alvarez: curious about egress \u2014 we need all model telemetry to stay in region, and any telemetry forwarded to our SIEM must go over private link. is that supported?
[03:35] Diego Ramos: telemetry can be routed to your endpoints; we can configure VPC endpoints to push logs to your Kinesis/Firehose or S3; region locality is configurable, we can avoid cross-region replication unless you opt in.
[03:50] Liam Chen: about IPs \u2014 how many ENIs per instance and do we need elastic IPs? we have strict limits per account.
[04:05] Diego Ramos: typical ENI usage is modest: control plane vs data plane, but if you use multi-tenant endpoints you'll have fewer ENIs; dedicated pools may create more ENIs per node. we can provide expected ENI/IP usage matrix based on instance types \u2014 we'll send you a spreadsheet.
[04:27] Maya Patel: action: diego will send ENI/IP guidance and terraform snippets.
[04:34] Priya Nair: region constraints: we operate in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 primarily. can redwood run in those regions for private?
[04:45] Diego Ramos: yes both supported; some latest GPU types may only be in select regions \u2014 if you need specific instance families we should check availability. also note Azure/GCP differences if you have hybrid clouds.
[05:05] Liam Chen: Transit Gateway \u2014 we prefer attaching via TGW. does Redwood support TGW attachments?
[05:15] Diego Ramos: yes, we can use TGW; pattern is Redwood's account attaches into your TGW or we deploy a customer-managed account. we also support AWS PrivateLink if you want to limit route table changes. there's tradeoffs: peering/TGW gives you full routability and can be better for internal service mesh traffic; PrivateLink/endpoint locks it down to service-level access.
[05:40] Sofia Alvarez: SSO and RBAC \u2014 do you integrate with our IdP for admin UIs?
[05:48] Maya Patel: we support SAML SSO and can map groups to RBAC roles. audit logs for admin actions can be exported.
[05:57] Priya Nair: any customer-managed key rotation requirements? we rotate keys monthly; curious how Redwood handles re-encryption of persisted caches.
[06:10] Diego Ramos: we support KMS keys with rotation; for caches we can use envelope encryption and rotate without full rewrites usually. we'll share specifics; sometimes reencryption is needed depending on storage backends.
[06:30] Liam Chen: curious about model artifact storage \u2014 where are models stored in private deploy?
[06:39] Diego Ramos: models can be stored in your S3 buckets, or in our encrypted storage within your VPC depending on deployment. for private on-prem we keep everything local.
[06:55] Maya Patel: price checkpoint \u2014 for proof of concept you can run a small dedicated pool or try hosted with private endpoint; pricing varies a lot by GPU family and reserved commit. we'll include a sample pricing scenario.
[07:12] Priya Nair: network team question: do you require route table changes in our production subnets? we prefer not to touch prod routes.
[07:25] Diego Ramos: you can isolate by using dedicated subnets for inference and attach route entries there; we avoid touching your prod route tables. with PrivateLink you mainly create interfaces in specific subnets.
[07:40] Liam Chen: does Redwood support cross-account role assumption for provisioning? our infra team won't hand over admin creds.
[07:49] Diego Ramos: yes, cross-account IAM roles are standard; we use limited-scope IAM roles, and Terraform can be run from a service account in your org.
[08:05] Sofia Alvarez: can we enforce FIPS endpoints and restrict crypto suites?
[08:12] Diego Ramos: depending on cloud provider we can route through FIPS endpoints or require TLS policies; for at-rest crypto we defer to your KMS and can support FIPS-certified HSMs if your provider has them.
[08:30] Maya Patel: ok quick check \u2014 priorities: 1) no public egress, 2) customer-managed KMS, 3) region locality, 4) audit logs to SIEM. correct?
[08:42] Priya Nair: correct.
[08:45] Liam Chen: timeline \u2014 we're hoping to start a pilot by mid-september and a rollout by end of year. can you support that?
[08:55] Maya Patel: yes that's the typical timeline for POC -> pilot -> dedicated commit. we'll pare the steps.
[09:05] Diego Ramos: technical note on latency \u2014 if you place workloads in your region the token latency is typically single-digit ms per token difference compared to our hosted region, but exacts depend on GPU packing and batch sizes. we'll run benchmarks in your region during the POC.
[09:25] Sofia Alvarez: about model versioning and rollouts \u2014 can we pin model versions and do canary rollouts within private deployment?
[09:35] Diego Ramos: yes, rollouts and pinning supported. we also support automatic fallback to a smaller model if latency/SLOs degrade.
[09:48] Priya Nair: terraform snippets would be great \u2014 we run infra-as-code.
[09:53] Diego Ramos: we'll include examples for peering, endpoint creation, and IAM role setup.
[10:05] Maya Patel: any competitors you're evaluating?
[10:09] Priya Nair: we are looking at aws bedrock for managed endpoints and a couple self-host vendors, and anthropic for model options.
[10:18] Maya Patel: good to know \u2014 we'll send comparison notes.
[10:25] Liam Chen: security deep dive \u2014 can diego and sofia set a time next week?
[10:30] Sofia Alvarez: yes, next week mornings work best (PST).
[10:35] Maya Patel: ok i'll coordinate calendar invites.
[10:40] Diego Ramos: any specific audit artifact formats you need for SOC2?
[10:44] Sofia Alvarez: iso and SOC2 Type II reports, plus encrypt key attestation and KMS logs.
[10:52] Diego Ramos: we'll surface our SOC2 docs and the KMS integration guide.
[11:00] Priya Nair: one last question: if we run in two regions, how do you handle replication? we prefer not to replicate training data cross-region.
[11:10] Diego Ramos: replication is opt-in; you can keep model artifacts and KV caches region-local. cross-region fallbacks are configurable but disabled by default.
[11:25] Maya Patel: great. recap and next steps: maya to send pricing and kickoff doc; diego to send terraform and ENI/IP matrix and schedule tech deep dive; sofia to share CIDR/RBAC needs and SOC2 checklist.
[11:45] Liam Chen: thanks all, clear path forward.
[11:50] Maya Patel: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials.
[11:55] Call end.
